questions.question: What does a tractor protection valve do?

options.text: It keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak.
It prevents the truck from being stolen.
It prevents the driver from going too fast.
It prevents the trailer from being accidentally released.

questions.correctAnswerText: It keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak.
questions.explanation: The tractor protection valve keeps air in the tractor or truck brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a leak.

questions.question: What should you do to help prevent rollovers?

options.text: Speed up quickly after stopping.
Drive slowly around turns.
Keep the load near the back of the trailer.
Keep the load on one side of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly around turns.
questions.explanation: To reduce the risk of rollover, keep cargo low to the ground and take curves and corners slowly.

questions.question: When connecting a trailer, what should you do?

options.text: Connect matching glad hands.
Any glad hand can be connected to any other glad hand.
Leave one glad hand unattached.
Connect only one set of glad hands.

questions.correctAnswerText: Connect matching glad hands.
questions.explanation: Connect matching glad hands. They are often color-coded to help drivers avoid mistakes. Blue is usually for service lines and red is usually for emergency lines.

questions.question: When do rollovers happen?

options.text: When a truck driver is driving too fast.
When the driver ahead is moving too slowly.
When a truck driver is driving too slowly.
When ABS is working effectively.

questions.correctAnswerText: When a truck driver is driving too fast.
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when a vehicle is driven too fast. To reduce rollover risk, load cargo low to the ground and take turns and curves slowly.

questions.question: What is the service air line attached to?

options.text: Relay valves.
Supply line.
Emergency air line.
Steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relay valves.
questions.explanation: The service air line carries air controlled by the foot brake or trailer hand brake. It is attached to relay valves, which allow the trailer brakes to work quickly.

questions.question: What should you know about driving a bobtail tractor?

options.text: Bobtails stop very easily.
Bobtails cannot drive as fast as tractors with trailers.
Bobtails are harder to stop than tractors with trailers.
Bobtails are illegal in most states.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bobtails are harder to stop than tractors with trailers.
questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor is not attached to a trailer. When driving a bobtail, know that it takes longer to stop and requires more distance than a tractor with a loaded trailer.

questions.question: When does a large combination vehicle take the longest to stop?

options.text: When fully loaded.
When partially loaded.
When empty.
When mostly loaded.

questions.correctAnswerText: When empty.
questions.explanation: Large combination vehicles take longer to stop when empty than when loaded. Less weight means less grip on the road.

questions.question: In a double or triple trailer combination, how should you position the trailers?

options.text: Spread cargo weight evenly between all trailers.
Put the heaviest trailer right behind the cab.
Put the heaviest trailer in the rear.
Trailer weight does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the heaviest trailer right behind the cab.
questions.explanation: The heaviest-loaded trailer should be closest to the tractor. The lightest trailer should be in the rear.

questions.question: Before backing under the trailer, what should you do with the trailer brakes?

options.text: Disengage them.
Lock them.
Deactivate them.
Dry them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lock them.
questions.explanation: Before backing your tractor under the trailer, lock the trailer brakes. This is an important step in safely coupling trailers.

questions.question: How can you best recognize when your trailer starts to skid?

options.text: By looking at other drivers' faces.
By seeing it in your mirrors.
By feeling it.
By listening to the radio.

questions.correctAnswerText: By seeing it in your mirrors.
questions.explanation: The best way to recognize the start of a trailer skid is to see the trailer moving off-course in your mirrors.

questions.question: What happens when a vehicle has ABS on only one axle?

options.text: Braking does not change.
It is not possible.
The driver has more control when braking.
It puts extra strain on the other axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver has more control when braking.
questions.explanation: Having ABS on just one axle or on the trailer gives the driver more control when braking.

questions.question: What do you test by pulling out the trailer air supply control?

options.text: The parking brake.
The trailer emergency brakes.
The trailer service brakes.
The landing gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer emergency brakes.
questions.explanation: Test the trailer emergency brakes before each trip. Pull out the trailer air supply control or move it to the emergency position. Pull forward with the tractor and make sure the trailer does not move.

questions.question: When backing a trailer, which way should you turn the steering wheel?

options.text: Turn the top of the steering wheel toward where you want the trailer to go.
Turn the top of the steering wheel away from where you want the trailer to go.
Direction does not matter.
It depends on where you are backing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the top of the steering wheel away from where you want the trailer to go.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, turn the top of the steering wheel away from where you want to go. Once the trailer starts turning, turn the steering wheel the other direction to follow the trailer.

questions.question: What should you do after finishing a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Close the service line valve.
Remove the service line valve.
Leave the emergency line valve open.
Leave the rear shut-off valves open.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close the service line valve.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, open the rear emergency line and service line shut-off valves to check for escaping air. Close both valves before you start driving.

questions.question: What is one way to prevent a rollover?

options.text: Move cargo to the left side of the rig.
Keep cargo centered on the rig.
Move cargo to the right side of the rig.
Keep cargo as far from the ground as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep cargo centered on the rig.
questions.explanation: Uneven cargo loading can cause a rollover. Always keep cargo centered on the rig to help prevent rollovers.

questions.question: Driving a combination vehicle ____ than driving a single vehicle.

options.text: Is easier
Requires more skill
Is better for training
Is safer in bad weather

questions.correctAnswerText: Requires more skill
questions.explanation: Driving a combination vehicle requires more skill than driving a single vehicle. Combination vehicles are longer and heavier.

questions.question: What can happen when you change lanes quickly?

options.text: A crack-the-whip effect that causes a rollover.
The trailer straightens out.
Other drivers get confused about which lane you are using.
Other drivers slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: A crack-the-whip effect that causes a rollover.
questions.explanation: The crack-the-whip effect from rearward amplification can cause a rollover when you change lanes too quickly in a combination vehicle.

questions.question: When is a trailer most likely to swing around?

options.text: When it is full.
When traveling in a straight line.
When it is empty.
When the wheels are rotating.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is empty.
questions.explanation: An empty trailer takes longer to stop than a loaded one. An empty or lightly loaded trailer is most likely to swing out and hit other vehicles.

questions.question: Why is proper coupling technique important?

options.text: It is the same for all vehicles.
It is essential for safe operation.
It means the fifth wheel plate should not be greased.
You can learn it over time.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is essential for safe operation.
questions.explanation: Proper coupling and uncoupling technique is critical for safe operation of combination vehicles. Improper coupling is very dangerous.

questions.question: How should you brake in a tractor-trailer with ABS?

options.text: Brake harder than normal.
Use extra braking force to activate the ABS.
Brake the same way you normally would.
Use less braking pressure than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake the same way you normally would.
questions.explanation: In a tractor-trailer with ABS, brake the same way you would in a vehicle without ABS.
